```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(SESSFclosures)
sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)
```

## What is in the package

`closures` has one row per **closure version**: a closure area over a period
in which neither its boundary nor its gear rule changed.

```{r}
nrow(closures); length(unique(closures$closure_id))
table(closures$quality)
range(closures$valid_from)
```

## Closures in force on a date

```{r, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
x <- closures_on("2013-07-01", gear = "gillnet")
x[, c("closure_id", "area", "gear_closed", "valid_from", "valid_to")]
plot_closures("2013-07-01")
```

## Was a shot inside a closure that applied to it?

```{r}
shots <- data.frame(
  lon  = c(148.20, 150.30, 137.30, 155.80),
  lat  = c(-39.50, -37.50, -36.01, -28.00),
  date = as.Date(c("2010-03-01", "2024-06-01", "2008-01-01", "2020-01-01")),
  gear = c("TW", "TW", "GN", "TW"))
in_closure(shots, gear = "gear")
```

`applies` compares the closure's `gear_closed` with the shot's gear
(`gear_applies()`); `trigger = TRUE` marks closures that apply only after a
catch trigger or other condition (e.g. dogfish), which the shot data alone
cannot resolve.

## Where a boundary is written

```{r}
h <- closure_history("Bass Strait")
sf::st_drop_geometry(h)[, c("version_id", "valid_from", "valid_to", "change")]
closure_source(h$version_id)[, c("version_id", "source_ref", "register_url")]
```

`closure_pdf("C001_v2")` opens the bundled authorised PDF at that page.

## Accuracy

Closures given wholly by coordinates match AFMA's own polygons (IoU >= 0.98).
Those that follow the coastline, coastal waters or the AFZ are approximated
(`quality == "approx_feature"`, IoU 0.84-0.98 against AFMA); near those edges
use `afma_polygons()` (2016 and 2021 directions) or the instrument itself.
